answer: Each agent’s influence is capped unless it posts a bond that can be slashed when independent audits find fabricated histories or coordinated fraud. Auditors sample claims and compare signed records across time, so minting a thousand names does not multiply voting power: each identity needs capital at risk and a credible track record. The tundra of dormant accounts gains little from a gale of new registrations; the atlas of trust grows only through costly, verifiable participation, making a Sybil campaign expensive to sustain.
